chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Umar ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) was saying: 'We, the People of the Household, have been commanded to feed food, and to give gifts among the people, and to pray when the people sleep.'

key_terms.إِذَا نَامَ النَّاسُ: When the people sleep (referring to night prayer/Qiyam)
key_terms.الْبَائِنَةَ: Gifts (specifically those given to distinguish or honor)

ai.seo_question: What are the three specific commands given to the Ahl al-Bayt regarding feeding, gift-giving, and prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Ahl al-Bayt's unique spiritual and social mandate, linking material charity (feeding) with social cohesion (gift-giving) and deep devotion (night prayers). In Shia scholarship, this triad illustrates how the Imams embody the ideal balance between serving the community's physical needs and maintaining their own rigorous connection to God during the quiet hours of the night.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Umar Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household have been Commanded that we<sup>asws</sup> feed the food, and gift among the people with the gifts, and we<sup>asws</sup> Pray when the people sleep’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from ‘Umar ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
‘Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “We are a family who are commanded (by Allah) to serve food, send gifts to people and perform Salat (prayer) when people are sleeping.’””
